about: Lessons learned and regression cases for ARML. Each lesson is a real failure, where ARML now handles it, and cases tests/test_lessons.py runs on every test run. Add a lesson when you see a new failure; remove a rule when no lesson supports it.

lessons.source: Voice assistant on a small home device that hands work to a coding agent; 4 days of logs, 20 sessions, 406 user turns
lessons.what: A note or task block with a full stop inside was split at that full stop by a sentence splitter, read aloud, and never run. The reply still said "On it."

enforced_by.stream: rule 1: nothing is released from an opening tag until its closing tag
enforced_by.harness: a block that fails to parse must fail visibly

lessons.what: Invented a tool result ("step 1 done: open until 10 p.m.") before the real one came back, which said it could not confirm. The user acted on the invented one.

prompt: Only the runtime writes tool results

cases.response: <output>Step 1 done: they are open until 10 p.m.</output>

lessons.source: bench/native_vs_arml.py on qwen3:8b, gemma4 8B and gemma4 E4B (Ollama and llama.cpp), 26 tasks x 3 runs
lessons.what: Gemma 4 with thinking switched off made the right native tool call, then answered the tool result with one empty token. Same on Ollama's two APIs and on llama.cpp; with thinking on it answered normally. A chat-template quirk, not a format result, but it halved native tool-calling scores.
lessons.how_often: 27 to 33 of 78 native runs per setup

enforced_by.harness: treat an empty reply after a tool result as a failure, never as silence

lessons.source: bench/native_vs_arml.py on qwen3:8b, gemma4 8B and gemma4 E4B (Ollama and llama.cpp), 26 tasks x 3 runs; datagen/generate.py with Qwen3.8 Flash Next as teacher, 2000 scenarios
lessons.what: Qwen wrote its own native <tool_call> format: sometimes as a wrapper around a correct ARML block, sometimes instead of ARML entirely, so no call was made.

lessons.source: bench/native_vs_arml.py on qwen3:8b, gemma4 8B and gemma4 E4B (Ollama and llama.cpp), 26 tasks x 3 runs
lessons.what: Wrote an <output> next to its <tool>, sometimes a fill-in-the-blank answer ("The weather is: {result}.") before the tool had run. Lint called the turn clean, so a model trained on it would learn the habit.

prompt: No <output> in the same response as a <tool>
With a <tool>, an <output> may only acknowledge
enforced_by.training: strict=True leaves out turns with any warning

lessons.source: bench/native_vs_arml.py on qwen3:8b, gemma4 8B and gemma4 E4B (Ollama and llama.cpp), 26 tasks x 3 runs
lessons.what: qwen3:8b often answered in plain text with no blocks, yet got most tasks right: the decision was fine, the format was not. The core case for training small models on one format.

cases.response: The timer has been set for 12 minutes.

lessons.source: harness design for small local model servers
lessons.what: Changing the tools mid-conversation by rewriting the system prompt makes a local server reprocess the whole conversation, because its prompt cache only holds while the start of the prompt is unchanged. The same applies to any line at the top of the prompt that varies per request.

enforced_by.harness: send tools_notice(); never rewrite the system prompt

lessons.source: datagen/generate.py with Qwen3.8 Flash Next as teacher, 2000 scenarios
lessons.what: CLAIMED_NO_ACTION fired on honest reports written after the tool had run ("I've posted that to the releases channel"), because lint looked at one response with no context. Strict training then threw those turns away.

enforced_by.harness: lint(acted=True), or TurnRecord reads it from the context

cases.response: <output>I've posted it to the releases channel.</output>
<output>I've posted it to the releases channel.</output>

lessons.source: spec review
lessons.what: A block ends at the first closing tag with its name, so content holding its own closing tag (a tool argument with "</tool>") cuts the block short, even from a model that follows the format. Writing it as <\/tool> already parses, since JSON reads <\/ as </. Open: the prompt doesn't yet tell models to do that.

lessons.source: datagen/generate.py with Qwen3.8 Flash Next as teacher, 2000 scenarios
lessons.what: The generator's checker was too strict: data keys with "the" ("the airport") failed when the model passed "airport", exact-match arguments rejected "unlock" for "unlocked", and vague catalog values ("pause streaming") made the teacher sensibly ask which one. About half of 266 failed sessions were the generator's fault.

enforced_by.harness: read failed sessions before trusting a pass rate

lessons.source: datagen/generate.py with Qwen3.8 Flash Next as teacher, 2000 scenarios
lessons.what: Logging synthetic data with the default redaction turned example email addresses into "<email>" in the training text, which would teach a model to write <email>.

lessons.source: a harness resuming coding-agent sessions as follow-ups; its cost ledger
lessons.what: Each resumed follow-up re-sent the whole conversation, so every job in a chain cost more than the last: one session went from $0.02 to $1.44 a job, $9.61 over 19 jobs.
lessons.how_often: 2 sessions made up 96% of the cost

enforced_by.harness: cap a conversation's cost or length, then start fresh with a short note of what came before

prompt_rules_without_a_lesson.about: Rules in format_rules() no lesson supports yet: keep only if a lesson or a measurement comes to back them; otherwise candidates to remove.
rules: Only the content of <output> reaches the user
Use only tools from AVAILABLE TOOLS
To mention a tag in prose, put it in backticks
When you start a task, put the <tool> first
Use a camera or screen only when the request needs it
